text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Record sales of hardwood furniture in Norway is contributing to the destruction of rainforests in Asia, the Rainforest Fund says. Furniture businesses admit they are not efficient in controlling where the wood comes from.
- The tax office and many tax inspectors have broken regulations by sending out tax notices too late. Every year thousands of tax payers and companies are reported to the authorities because of this.
- Terms and conditions for conscription are to be improved to enhance motivation. Conscripts opting for civilian service will also get a better deal.
- Norway was the first country to develop a bourse for electricity and a free power market. The experience has now become a lucrative export product.
- International flights to and from Norway increased by 15.3 percent in the first half of the year compared with the same period in 1996. Domestic traffic grew by 4.9 percent.

- Thirty years after developing a weapon control system for submarines, Kongsberg Group has made an international breakthrough. The company could possibly land a 300 million crown contract with an Italian shipyard.

- SpareBank 1 Midt-Norge has written down its stake in Fokus Bank by 30 million crowns following the failed attempt in the spring of the Sparebankgruppen group of savings banks to take over Fokus Bank, Norway's third largest commercial bank.
- Finn Hvistendahl, head of Den norske Bank (DnB), wants to open a branch in Murmansk and will soon apply to Russian and Norwegian authorities for a concession.

- Norway will suffer from a chronic shortfall in the labour market in the next century, says Ragnar Johansen, head of research at the Labour Research Institute. The Labour Directorate put unemployment at 3.6 percent in July.

- The market value of software house Computer Advances Group (CAG) rose by 60 million crowns, or 20 percent, on Thursday after the company announced a distribution agreement with U.S. media group Media-Tech for radio station data systems. The share price rose in spite of the fact that CAG is not guaranteed an income from the deal.
